what_it_does: Alerts for AI agents that go rogue. The operator sends OpenTelemetry call metadata, KYDE learns each agent's baseline, scores new records from 0 to 100 with its open-source drift detectors (https://github.com/kydehq/behavioral-drift-detection) and calls a webhook when an agent's score band changes, with the reason and a signed score. Deterministic statistics, no LLM in the scoring path.

body.webhook_url: <https URL that receives alerts: Slack, Discord or your own endpoint>

get_key.note: KYDE first sends a test message to the webhook, so nobody can register someone else's endpoint.

send_telemetry.registering_agents: Nothing to register. Each agent is identified by its OpenTelemetry service.name and appears with its first data. One key covers all agents.

webhook.when: An agent's score band changes, after a baseline of 30 runs.
webhook.signature: Kyde-Signature header: t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp and body, keyed with your key>
webhook.retries: Non-2xx responses are retried. Schedule: xxx
webhook.slack_and_discord: Slack and Discord webhook URLs receive a formatted message instead of raw JSON.

example.explain: Called upload_file 14 times in run_8812. Baseline: never.

how_content_stays_local: Delete or hash content attributes in the operator's OpenTelemetry Collector before export (attributes processor, delete and hash actions).
own_infrastructure: On-prem or private cloud with the same detectors: talk to us.

demo.note: Synthetic agents, signed with a demo key. Not real customers.
